question: Can the effect of passage-coherent context triples be separated from the effects of triple ordering and serialization format that other work attributes gains to?
description: doi:10.20944/preprints202505.1992.v1 reports that ordering triplets (BFS) and merging redundant overlapping subgraphs improves answer precision, while arxiv:2609.10237 reports that syntax, triple order and subgraph size produce no measurable effect at multi-hop depth. Given that at least one retrieved paper attributes gains to ordering/serialization of the context triples, any observed gain from the idea's context-augmented regime could be an ordering/formatting artefact rather than passage coherence. The idea's ablation must hold serialization and triple order fixed (or explicitly vary them) to attribute gains to passage provenance.
rationale: Two retrieved papers make opposing claims about whether order/serialization matter, so the idea's ablation design must neutralize this dimension or the context-enrichment effect will be uninterpretable.
